title: He became the first Indian-American founder to take a company public on Nasdaq - after fifty investors said no.
sources: Wikipedia - Kanwal Rekhi biography, Excelan founding and 1987 Nasdaq IPO
American Bazaar, 2026 - Meet Kanwal Rekhi: first Indian founder to list on Nasdaq
caption:
He became the first Indian-American founder to take a company public on Nasdaq - after fifty investors said no.

An IIT Bombay graduate, Rekhi moved to the US in the early 1970s and co-founded Excelan, a Silicon Valley networking hardware company, at a time when almost no Indian founders were raising venture money.

In 1987, Rekhi took Excelan public on Nasdaq - the first Indian-American founder and CEO to take a venture-backed company public on a US stock exchange. Excelan later merged with Novell, where Rekhi became EVP and CTO.

Rekhi went on to co-found TiE - The Indus Entrepreneurs - now the world's largest network of Indian and South Asian entrepreneurs. One IPO opened a door; building TiE made sure the door stayed open for everyone who came after.
